title: Impact of FDA Drug Approval on Biotech Company Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
**Event Study methodology** is appropriate here. This is a classic event study analyzing market reactions to FDA drug approvals. The key assumption is that in the absence of the FDA approval event, stock returns would follow their normal relationship with market returns (captured by the market model). We identify the causal effect by comparing actual returns around the event date to predicted "normal" returns from the pre-event estimation window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s63_data.csv")

# Event study analysis
perform_event_study <- function(data) {
  # Define windows
  estimation_start <- -250
  estimation_end <- -11
  event_start <- -10
  event_end <- 10
  
  results <- data %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    arrange(event_day) %>%
    summarise(
      # Calculate abnormal returns for each day
      abnormal_returns = list({
        # Get estimation period data (assuming we have it, or use available pre-event data)
        est_data <- data.frame(
          ret = ret[event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -1],
          mkt_ret = mkt_ret[event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -1]
        )
        
        # Simple market model using beta
        beta_val <- unique(beta)[1]
        
        # Calculate abnormal returns for event window
        event_data <- data.frame(
          event_day = event_day[event_day >= event_start & event_day <= event_end],
          ret = ret[event_day >= event_start & event_day <= event_end],
          mkt_ret = mkt_ret[event_day >= event_start & event_day <= event_end]
        )
        
        # Abnormal return = Actual return - (Beta * Market return)
        event_data$abnormal_ret <- event_data$ret - (beta_val * event_data$mkt_ret)
        
        event_data
      }),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  # Calculate average abnormal returns by event day
  all_abnormal <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:length(results$abnormal_returns), function(i) {
    df <- results$abnormal_returns[[i]]
    df$stock_id <- results$stock_id[i]
    df
  }))
  
  # Average abnormal returns by day
  aar <- all_abnormal %>%
    group_by(event_day) %>%
    summarise(
      AAR = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_stocks = n(),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  return(list(individual = all_abnormal, average = aar))
}

# Run event study
event_results <- perform_event_study(data)

# Calculate key metrics
aar_data <- event_results$average

# Calculate Cumulative Average Abnormal Returns (CAAR)
aar_data$CAAR <- cumsum(aar_data$AAR)

# Key event windows
cat("=== EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Average Abnormal Return on Event Day (day 0):\n")
event_day_aar <- aar_data$AAR[aar_data$event_day == 0]
if(length(event_day_aar) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("AAR[0] = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", event_day_aar, event_day_aar * 100))
} else {
  cat("Event day 0 not found in data\n")
}

# 3-day window around event [-1, +1]
window_3day <- aar_data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  summarise(CAR_3day = sum(AAR, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(CAR_3day)

cat(sprintf("3-day CAR [-1,+1] = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", window_3day, window_3day * 100))

# 5-day window around event [-2, +2]
window_5day <- aar_data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= -2 & event_day <= 2) %>%
  summarise(CAR_5day = sum(AAR, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(CAR_5day)

cat(sprintf("5-day CAR [-2,+2] = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", window_5day, window_5day * 100))

# Post-event window [0, +5]
post_event <- aar_data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= 0 & event_day <= 5) %>%
  summarise(CAR_post = sum(AAR, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(CAR_post)

cat(sprintf("Post-event CAR [0,+5] = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", post_event, post_event * 100))

# Statistical significance test (simple t-test)
individual_cars <- event_results$individual %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_3day = sum(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

t_test_result <- t.test(individual_cars$CAR_3day, mu = 0)
cat(sprintf("3-day CAR t-statistic: %.3f (p-value: %.4f)\n", 
            t_test_result$statistic, t_test_result$p.value))

# Robustness check: Market-adjusted returns (alternative to beta-adjusted)
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK: Market-Adjusted Returns ===\n")
market_adjusted <- data %>%
  mutate(abnormal_ret_ma = ret - mkt_ret) %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(AAR_ma = mean(abnormal_ret_ma, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

car_ma_3day <- sum(market_adjusted$AAR_ma, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Market-adjusted 3-day CAR [-1,+1] = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", 
            car_ma_3day, car_ma_3day * 100))

# Plot results
cat("\n=== VISUALIZATION ===\n")
print(ggplot(aar_data, aes(x = event_day)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y = AAR), stat = "identity", fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = CAAR), color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Average Abnormal Returns and Cumulative CAR",
       subtitle = "FDA Drug Approval Event Study",
       x = "Event Day", y = "Return") +
  theme_minimal())

cat("Analysis complete.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect **positive abnormal returns** around FDA approval announcements, particularly on the event day and immediately after. The magnitude should be **3-8% cumulative abnormal returns** in the 3-day window around the event. This is because FDA drug approvals represent significant positive news that increases the expected future cash flows of biotech companies. The market reaction should be strongest on the announcement day (day 0) with some potential anticipation effects in the day before and continuation effects in the days following. Biotech stocks are typically more volatile and sensitive to regulatory news compared to other sectors, so the magnitude could be on the higher end of this range.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the timing of FDA drug approval announcements as a natural experiment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: FDA drug approvals lead to a positive change in biotech companies' CAR.
